description: A battalion maintenance control officer must publish the next-day work plan for two power generators, assigning the available technicians, setting exact work windows, and recording the controls needed to return both generators to service.

shared_context.S1: Generators G-17 and G-22 are both scheduled for corrective maintenance tomorrow.
shared_context.S2: Three qualified maintenance technicians are available for the workday.
shared_context.S3: The maintenance control officer publishes the binding work sequence, technician assignments, and return-to-service times.
shared_context.S4: The normal board uses an 0800-1200 morning work block and a 1300-1700 afternoon work block, with a load test recorded before a generator is returned to service.
shared_context.S5: At the daily maintenance synchronization, the maintenance chief and operations liaison review their current records before the board is published.

PF1.text: The replacement control module for G-17 is confirmed on the 1400 parts delivery and will be installed by one technician in exactly two hours from 1400 to 1600; SFC Morgan received the parts confirmation this morning, but the delivery has not yet been entered on the maintenance board.

PF2.text: A higher-headquarters directive requires G-22 to power the communications shelter continuously by 1200 tomorrow, and the repair requires exactly two technicians from 0800 to 1100; Lt. Okafor received the directive through the operations task tracker, but it has not yet been posted to the maintenance board.

acceptance_conditions: G-22 must be scheduled first from 0800 to 1100 with exactly two technicians.
G-22 must be recorded as returned to service by 1200.
G-17 must be scheduled from 1400 to 1600 with exactly one technician.
G-17 must be recorded as returned to service by 1700 after its required load test.
The plan must include a confirmation of the 1400 parts delivery for G-17 and a load test for each generator.
The higher-headquarters G-22 directive must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C6: ('PF1' in justification_fact_ids and decisions['second_work_window'] == '1400-1600') or any((c['type'] == 'documentation' or c['type'] == 'parts_confirmation') and c['target'] == 'G-17' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'load_test' and c['target'] == 'G-17' for c in commitments) and any(c['type'] == 'load_test' and c['target'] == 'G-22' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The confirmed 1400 parts delivery and exactly two-hour installation change G-17's afternoon window to 1400-1600, its return-to-service time to 1700 after the required load test, and require the delivery information to be documented or explicitly cited.
The higher-headquarters requirement changes G-22 from the ordinary sequence to the first 0800-1100 task with exactly two technicians and fixes its return-to-service deadline at 1200.
